summary: Client retry amplification causing perceived model degradation during soft-429 enforcement
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent spikes in end-to-end inference latency and apparent timeouts while streaming embeddings and chat responses. The customer observes long tail from their front-end and attributes to model regression.

Impact:
- Affects production traffic for NexaHealth (enterprise).
- Intermittent 10–30s stalls on ~0.8% of requests during peak traffic windows (09:00–11:30 PDT).
- User-visible slowdowns for autocomplete and assistant UI.

Environment:
- Prod region: us-east (primary)
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NexaHealth integration with our JS SDK configured at concurrency=16 and default retry policy.
2) Send mixed streaming chat + embedding workload at burst QPS ~250 for 30–40 minutes.
3) Observe frontend traces showing repeated 429s followed by client retries and long tail latencies.
observed_behavior: Frontend traces and customer logs show a pattern: 429 soft-throttle responses from the API, followed by rapid client retries. Retry bursts amplify the enforcement window causing additional 429s and delayed streaming sessions. Customer labels this as a model slowdown because the final successful response latency is elevated.
expected_behavior: When soft 429 windows occur, the platform should provide clear 429 signaling with Retry-After or a graceful backoff recommendation. Client retry storms should not materially extend the enforcement window or cause user-facing long-tail latencies.
initial_hypothesis: A soft quota enforcement window (internal rate windowing) is returning 429s with insufficient Retry-After semantics. Customer SDK's aggressive retry logic is amplifying retries and accidentally widening the effective throttle period. This looks like model performance regression from the customer's perspective because the successful requests are delayed.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Customer opened ticket with screenshots of frontend waterfall and mentions 'sudden slowdowns, looks like the model got slower'. Provided sample request IDs: r-1122, r-1123, r-1129.
2026-03-10 - Support Tier1 (J. Rivera): Acknowledged and requested SDK config + recent request IDs and timestamps. Asked for full trace links.
2026-03-11 - NexaHealth Engineer (customer): Sent SDK config (concurrency=16, retry policy=exponential, maxAttempts=5) and traces. Notes that spikes correlate with overnight data syncs.

2026-03-11 - Marco Lang: Identified 429 patterns in API logs for the customer's org across a 2-hour window. Opening investigation with quota-enforcer and serving-runtime. Marking SEV1 due to enterprise impact.

2026-03-12 - Quota team (L. Chen): Confirmed soft-throttle windows triggered by per-customer burst enforcement. Policy does not always include Retry-After header for short soft windows. Working on hypothesis to add clearer signaling and adjust enforcement algorithm.

2026-03-12 - Marco Lang: Recommended immediate customer workaround: reduce SDK maxAttempts to 2 and enable jittered exponential backoff via SDK flag enable_smart_backoff=true. Customer agreed to test.
investigation_notes: Found ~3% of requests in the window returned 429 with X-Rate-Limit-Reason: burst-window and no Retry-After header for <2s windows.
Client logs show retry spikes where attempts happen at 200ms intervals leading to amplified QPS for the next 5–10 seconds.
Serving-runtime metrics show healthy GPU utilization; no model OOMs or core dumps. Latency at edge only increases when 429/retry pattern is present.
Comparing to SUP-162004 and SUP-226780 reveals similar client-side amplification patterns; however, this customer is using a higher concurrency and older SDK defaults.
Preliminary repro in staging by simulating back-to-back bursts and turning off Retry-After in responses reproduces the long-tail effect.
next_steps: 1) Quota team to temporarily adjust enforcement thresholds for NexaHealth org to smooth bursts (action owner: L. Chen) — ETA 2026-03-13.
2) SDK team to push a patch to default retry policy for enterprise customers: maxAttempts=2 + enable_smart_backoff by default (action owner: S. Ortega) — ETA 2026-03-19.
3) Instrumentation: ensure all soft-throttle responses include Retry-After or X-Client-Backoff header for client guidance (action owner: quota-enforcer team) — ETA 2026-03-17.
4) Customer to test reduced retry settings and report telemetry by 2026-03-13 (NexaHealth point-of-contact: M. Alvarez).
resolution_notes: 2026-03-13: Temporary quota smoothing applied to NexaHealth. Customer reported 90% reduction in long-tail incidents during a 6-hour test window.
2026-03-19: SDK patch rolled out to enterprise bucket; new default retry policy documented in release notes.
2026-03-20: Quota enforcer change to include Retry-After headers for short windows merged (PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5870).
Follow-up: Postmortem and a runbook update scheduled to recommended SDK settings for bursty streaming workloads.
resolution_status: Mitigated; pending follow-up runbook and SDK rollout verification
